title: Acts Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 20.

questions.question: In Acts 20, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul called unto him the disciples
Eutychus fell into a deep sleep
They brought the young man alive
questions.correctAnswer: Paul called unto him the disciples
questions.explanation: In Acts 20:1, it states that after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, making this the first event in the chapter.

questions.question: Where did Paul go after he had given much exhortation?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:2 states that after giving much exhortation, Paul came into Greece.

questions.question: For how long did Paul abide in Greece?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:3 specifies that Paul abode in Greece for three months.

questions.question: Who accompanied Paul into Asia?
questions.explanation: According to Acts 20:4, Timotheus is listed as one of those who accompanied Paul into Asia.

questions.question: What did the disciples do on the first day of the week?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:7 notes that the disciples came together to break bread on the first day of the week.

questions.question: At what time did Paul continue his speech until?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:7 states that Paul continued his speech until midnight.

questions.question: What happened to Eutychus during Paul's preaching?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:9 describes that Eutychus, after falling into a deep sleep, fell down from the third loft and was taken up dead.

questions.question: What did Paul do after he came down to Eutychus?
questions.explanation: In Acts 20:10, Paul went down, embraced Eutychus, and assured those present that his life was in him.

questions.question: What did they do after Eutychus was brought back to life?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:12 notes that after bringing the young man alive, they were not a little comforted.

questions.question: What did Paul intend to do instead of sailing into Syria?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:3 specifies that Paul purposed to return through Macedonia instead of sailing into Syria.

questions.question: How long did Paul and his companions stay in Troas?
questions.explanation: According to Acts 20:6, they abode in Troas for seven days.

questions.question: True or False: Paul preached until midnight.
questions.explanation: Acts 20:7 states that Paul continued his speech until midnight, making this statement true.

questions.question: True or False: Eutychus was sitting in a window when he fell asleep.
questions.explanation: Acts 20:9 confirms that Eutychus was sitting in a window when he fell into a deep sleep.

questions.question: True or False: Paul sailed directly to Syria without any plans to return through Macedonia.
questions.explanation: Acts 20:3 indicates that Paul purposed to return through Macedonia instead of sailing directly to Syria.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples gathered on the last day of the week.
questions.explanation: Acts 20:7 states that the disciples gathered on the first day of the week, not the last.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Where did Paul and his companions meet after sailing from Assos?
questions.explanation: They took him in and came to Mitylene as stated in Acts 20:14.

questions.question: What does Acts 20:15 promise will happen if someone sails from Mitylene?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:15 describes the journey from Mitylene to Samos, affirming the promise of arrival.

questions.question: Why did Paul choose to sail by Ephesus?
options: He was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem
He planned to return to Macedonia
questions.correctAnswer: He was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Acts 20:16 indicates that Paul hastened to be in Jerusalem for Pentecost, avoiding Ephesus.

questions.question: What did Paul do from Miletus?
options: Called the elders of the church
questions.correctAnswer: Called the elders of the church
questions.explanation: Acts 20:17 shows that Paul sent for the elders from Ephesus to meet him in Miletus.

questions.question: How did Paul describe his service among the people in Asia?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:19 notes that Paul served with humility, tears, and faced temptations.

questions.question: What did Paul keep back from the people?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:20 specifies that Paul did not hold back anything beneficial for the church.

questions.question: To whom did Paul testify during his ministry?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:21 confirms that Paul testified to both groups about repentance and faith.

questions.question: What was Paul's emotional state regarding his journey to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:22 illustrates Paul's determination to go to Jerusalem despite uncertainty.

questions.question: What did the Holy Ghost witness to Paul in every city?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:23 indicates that Paul was warned of the trials he would face in his journey.

questions.question: What was Paul's attitude towards his life in relation to his ministry?
options: He did not count it dear to himself
questions.correctAnswer: He did not count it dear to himself
questions.explanation: Acts 20:24 shows Paul's willingness to sacrifice for the purpose of completing his ministry.

questions.question: What did Paul know about the elders he spoke to?
options: They would see his face no more
questions.correctAnswer: They would see his face no more
questions.explanation: Acts 20:25 reveals that Paul understood this would be his final meeting with them.

questions.question: What declaration did Paul make about his ministry?
options: He was guilty of their blood
He was pure from the blood of all men
He had failed in his duties
questions.correctAnswer: He was pure from the blood of all men
questions.explanation: Acts 20:26 states that Paul took responsibility for faithfully preaching the gospel.

questions.question: True or False: Paul preached only to the Jews during his ministry.
questions.explanation: Acts 20:21 indicates that Paul preached to both Jews and Greeks.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was uncertain about what awaited him in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Acts 20:22 shows that Paul did not know what would happen to him in Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Paul planned to spend time in Ephesus during his journey.
questions.explanation: Acts 20:16 explains that Paul chose to sail by Ephesus to avoid spending time there.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 20.

questions.question: According to Acts 20:27, what did Paul not shun to declare unto the people?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:27 states, 'For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God,' indicating Paul proclaimed the full message of God's plan without omission.

questions.question: In Acts 20:28, to whom are the overseers instructed to take heed?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:28 commands, 'Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock,' highlighting the dual responsibility of church leaders for both personal and congregational care.

questions.question: What metaphor does Paul use in Acts 20:29 to describe those who will harm the church after his departure?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:29 says, 'For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you,' using the metaphor of wolves to denote dangerous enemies threatening the church.

questions.question: According to Acts 20:31, how long did Paul warn the people night and day with tears?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:31 states, 'by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears,' emphasizing the duration and intensity of Paul's ministry.

questions.question: What is Paul’s attitude towards material possessions as expressed in Acts 20:33?
options: I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel
I accept gifts from the wealthy
I seek gold and silver for ministry
questions.correctAnswer: I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel
questions.explanation: Acts 20:33 quotes Paul saying, 'I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel,' showing his refusal to seek personal gain from ministry.

questions.question: What saying of the Lord Jesus does Paul remind the Ephesian elders of in Acts 20:35?
options: It is more blessed to give than to receive
questions.correctAnswer: It is more blessed to give than to receive
questions.explanation: Acts 20:35 records Paul quoting Jesus' teaching, 'It is more blessed to give than to receive,' encouraging generosity and support for the weak.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Greek word 'overseers' (episkopos) in Acts 20:28?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'episkopos' in Acts 20:28 means 'bishops or guardians,' referring to those appointed to watch over and care for the church.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominent in Paul’s farewell speech to the Ephesian elders in Acts 20:17-38?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:17-38 shows inclusio by framing the speech with Paul’s arrival and the elders’ weeping departure (verses 17 and 38), creating a literary bookend that emphasizes the emotional farewell.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Paul’s warning about 'grievous wolves' in Acts 20:29?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 23:1-2 warns about shepherds who scatter the flock, paralleling Paul’s 'grievous wolves' metaphor in Acts 20:29 about harmful leaders threatening God’s people.

questions.question: The exhortation to 'support the weak' in Acts 20:35 connects to which New Testament teaching?
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:2 instructs believers to 'bear one another's burdens,' resonating with Paul’s teaching in Acts 20:35 about supporting the weak.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Paul's declaration in Acts 20:27 about not shunning to declare all the counsel of God?
options: Paul taking the Ephesian elders' attendance
Paul stating he is pure from the blood of all men
Paul warning about wolves entering the flock
Paul recounting his three years of ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Paul stating he is pure from the blood of all men
questions.explanation: Acts 20:26 immediately precedes 20:27 where Paul says, 'Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men,' setting context for his full declaration of God's counsel.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Acts 20:29-30 where Paul warns about external wolves and internal men arising?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:29-30 uses chiasm by contrasting external 'grievous wolves' with internal 'men arising' who speak perverse things, highlighting threats from both outside and inside the church.

questions.question: How does Paul’s statement in Acts 20:34 about his hands ministering to his necessities reflect wider Greco-Roman cultural values?
options: It reflects the virtue of self-sufficiency and honor in labor
It shows disdain for manual work
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the virtue of self-sufficiency and honor in labor
questions.explanation: Acts 20:34 illustrates Paul’s adherence to Greco-Roman values of self-sufficiency and honorable labor, as he worked to avoid being a burden and to set an example.

questions.question: What foreshadowing is present in Acts 20:22-23 regarding Paul’s journey to Jerusalem?
options: Paul will face bonds and afflictions
questions.correctAnswer: Paul will face bonds and afflictions
questions.explanation: Acts 20:22-23 foreshadows Paul's suffering by the Holy Spirit’s witness that bonds and afflictions await him in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Paul’s commendation of the elders to 'God, and to the word of his grace' in Acts 20:32 is an example of what?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:32 typologically commends believers to the sustaining power of God's word, which builds up and grants inheritance, linking spiritual nourishment to divine promise.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 20:24 teach about the believer's attitude toward life and ministry in the face of suffering?
options: The believer should value life above all to avoid suffering
The believer may count his life as dear but must endure suffering silently
The believer counts life as not dear and willingly embraces suffering to finish his ministry
The believer avoids suffering by abandoning ministry when threatened
questions.correctAnswer: The believer counts life as not dear and willingly embraces suffering to finish his ministry
questions.explanation: Acts 20:24 explicitly states Paul does not count his life dear to himself so that he may finish his course and ministry with joy, showing the doctrine of willing endurance of suffering for the gospel.

questions.question: What doctrine about the Holy Spirit's role in forewarning believers is taught in Acts 20:23?
options: The Holy Spirit only comforts and never warns
The Holy Spirit testifies universally about upcoming bonds and afflictions
The Holy Spirit guarantees safety from persecution
The Holy Spirit's witness is limited to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit testifies universally about upcoming bonds and afflictions
questions.explanation: Acts 20:23 teaches the Holy Ghost witnesses in every city that bonds and afflictions await Paul, showing the Spirit’s role in forewarning believers of coming trials.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the nature of pastoral responsibility is taught in Acts 20:28?
options: Pastors oversee the flock without divine appointment
The church belongs to the elders through human effort
The Holy Spirit appoints overseers to feed the church purchased by Christ’s blood
The flock is self-sustaining and requires no leadership
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit appoints overseers to feed the church purchased by Christ’s blood
questions.explanation: Acts 20:28 teaches that the Holy Ghost made the elders overseers to feed the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood, defining pastoral responsibility as divinely appointed and grounded in Christ’s atonement.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 20:22 specifically demonstrate regarding Paul's mission?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:22 shows Paul going 'bound in the spirit' to Jerusalem, submitting himself to God's sovereign will despite uncertainty, demonstrating divine sovereignty over his mission.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Acts 20:32 in the context of spiritual growth and inheritance?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:32 commends the believers to God and to the word of His grace, which is able to build them up and give them an inheritance among sanctified ones, highlighting God's grace.

questions.question: How does Acts 20:9–10 connect to the broader biblical theme of resurrection and divine power over death?
options: It denies resurrection and focuses on natural causes
It illustrates human ability to revive others without God
It demonstrates God’s power to restore life, foreshadowing Christ’s resurrection
It teaches that death is irreversible and final
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God’s power to restore life, foreshadowing Christ’s resurrection
questions.explanation: Acts 20:9–10 recounts Paul raising Eutychus from death, reflecting divine power over death and connecting to the ultimate resurrection in Christ, a major biblical theme.

questions.question: How does Paul’s farewell address in Acts 20:18–38 fulfill the theme of faithful apostolic ministry found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It contradicts earlier apostolic warnings by encouraging compromise
It exemplifies the shepherd-like care and warning against false teachers, consistent with pastoral epistles
It focuses only on personal achievements without regard for the church
It minimizes the importance of doctrine in favor of social unity
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the shepherd-like care and warning against false teachers, consistent with pastoral epistles
questions.explanation: Acts 20:18–38 shows Paul’s faithful ministry with humility, care, warnings about wolves, and exhortation to watchfulness, fulfilling the apostolic pastoral themes seen in the Pastoral Epistles.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Acts 20:27 and Acts 20:31 teach about apostolic proclamation and perseverance?
options: Apostles should avoid difficult teachings to maintain unity
Apostolic teaching includes shunning profitable counsel for safety
Apostles must declare all counsel of God and persevere in warning despite hardship
Apostles rely on human wisdom rather than divine revelation
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles must declare all counsel of God and persevere in warning despite hardship
questions.explanation: Acts 20:27 states Paul did not shun to declare all the counsel of God; 20:31 notes his ceaseless warnings with tears, teaching the doctrine of comprehensive proclamation and perseverance in ministry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 20:21 and Acts 20:24 teach about salvation and Christian mission?
options: Salvation is based on works, and mission is optional
Salvation requires repentance and faith, and mission is to testify joyfully despite suffering
Faith alone suffices without repentance, and mission is motivated by personal gain
Mission avoids suffering and focuses on cultural accommodation
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation requires repentance and faith, and mission is to testify joyfully despite suffering
questions.explanation: Acts 20:21 declares testimony of repentance toward God and faith in Jesus Christ; 20:24 emphasizes finishing ministry with joy despite trials, combining doctrines of salvation and mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Acts 20:28 and Acts 20:30 teach about church leadership and internal threats?
options: Church leaders are appointed by men and face no internal threats
The Holy Spirit appoints overseers who must guard against false teachers from within and without
Church leadership is optional and internal threats are minimal
Leaders should avoid confronting false teachers to maintain peace
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit appoints overseers who must guard against false teachers from within and without
questions.explanation: Acts 20:28 teaches the Holy Spirit appoints overseers to feed the church; 20:30 warns that men from within will arise speaking perverse things, showing leadership must protect the flock from internal and external dangers.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Paul’s raising of Eutychus (Acts 20:9–12) is a myth to embellish his ministry. What does Acts 20:9–12 actually teach?
options: Paul had no real power and the story is a fabricated legend
The event demonstrates divine power working through Paul, authenticating apostolic authority
The story is symbolic and not historical
The text suggests Eutychus remained dead despite Paul’s efforts
questions.correctAnswer: The event demonstrates divine power working through Paul, authenticating apostolic authority
questions.explanation: Acts 20:9–12 recounts Paul embracing the young man and declaring his life is in him, showing divine power validating Paul’s apostolic authority, not myth or symbolism.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian generosity and labor is taught in Acts 20:33–35?
options: Christian leaders should seek wealth and luxury
Believers should rely on others without personal labor
Christian labor supports the weak and giving is more blessed than receiving
Giving is optional and unrelated to Christian duty
questions.correctAnswer: Christian labor supports the weak and giving is more blessed than receiving
questions.explanation: Acts 20:33–35 teaches Paul labored to support himself and others, exhorting believers to support the weak and quoting Jesus that it is more blessed to give than to receive, highlighting generosity and work ethic.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 20:19 reveal through Paul’s ministry amid trials?
questions.explanation: Acts 20:19 describes Paul serving the Lord with humility and many tears despite temptations and threats, demonstrating God’s attribute of longsuffering working through him.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Paul’s travel plans in Acts 20:16 relate to the fulfillment of redemptive history?
options: Paul ignores Jewish festivals and focuses on Gentile ministry
Paul hastens to Jerusalem to participate in Pentecost, linking Gospel mission to Jewish feast fulfillment
Paul avoids Jerusalem to escape persecution
questions.correctAnswer: Paul hastens to Jerusalem to participate in Pentecost, linking Gospel mission to Jewish feast fulfillment
questions.explanation: Acts 20:16 states Paul’s determination to be at Jerusalem by Pentecost, connecting the Christian mission with Jewish redemptive history and the outpouring of the Spirit.

questions.question: What doctrine about apostolic humility and relational ministry is taught in Acts 20:18–20?
options: Apostles minister with arrogance and distance
Paul ministered with humility, tears, and from house to house
Apostolic ministry is impersonal and public only
questions.correctAnswer: Paul ministered with humility, tears, and from house to house
questions.explanation: Acts 20:18–20 records Paul’s humble service with many tears and personal teaching both publicly and house to house, teaching apostolic humility and relational ministry.
